petitpals.title: PetitPals Web & Extension
petitpals.subtitle: A full-stack universal baby registry ecosystem designed for the modern fragmented e-commerce landscape.

reach.label: Retailer Coverage
reach.desc: Universal compatibility with 100% of online storefronts.

onboarding.label: Time to First Action
onboarding.desc: Time from discovery to first meaningful user action.

sections.project_origin_content: PetitPals addresses the fragmented cart problem and dismantles retailer vendor lock-in where parents' desired items are scattered across niche boutiques, Etsy, and major retailers. The challenge was building a high-trust, decentralized source of truth that unifies these data points into a cohesive, aesthetically premium registry. By removing the friction of multi-site management, we bypass closed corporate ecosystems, transitioning users from a chaotic spreadsheet to a radical, liberating, and unified gifting experience.
sections.learning_objectives_content: My primary goals for PetitPals were to master Manifest V3 extension architectures and design a high-reliability data synchronization layer across disparate client states. I wanted to prove that a solo developer could build a seamless, cross-context product by combining non-destructive DOM manipulation with lightweight serverless databases, all while maintaining high data consistency without the overhead of heavy WebSockets.
sections.workplace_frustration_content: E-commerce fragmentation forces parents to navigate walled gardens—traditional registries like Vertbaudet deliberately lock users into their proprietary catalogs, punishing multi-store cross-shopping. Parents are forced to maintain 3 to 4 separate registries or track un-synchronized spreadsheets. For gift givers, this creates a broken user journey: navigating disparate external storefronts, manually cross-checking item availability, and encountering frustrating double-purchases.
behavioral_insights_list: 🛑 Proprietary retailer vendor lock-in (e.g., Vertbaudet closing ecosystem boundaries).
🛑 High fragmentation leading to 3-4 separate, un-synchronized spreadsheets.
🛑 Broken gift-giver journeys causing duplicate purchases and blind manual cross-checking.
sections.anonymity_challenge_content: A major friction point in traditional registries is the forced user registration for guest claims. Gift givers often abandon reservations when forced to create an account. I resolved this by engineering a frictionless guest checkout flow that allows item reservation using secure atomic transactions via Supabase RPCs, preventing claim collisions and guaranteeing data integrity without requiring user authentication.
sections.scoping_mvp_content: To deliver a functional solution rapidly, I scoped the MVP to two core components: a Chrome extension for one-click product scraping and a centralized, mobile-responsive dashboard for gift-givers. I deliberately postponed advanced registry features such as automated price-alert tracking and social sharing loops to focus on refining the core scraping and reservation engines.
sections.tech_debt_content: To bypass the overhead of orchestrating a dedicated WebSocket server for real-time synchronization, I leveraged Supabase's built-in Postgres CDC and client-side page visibility triggers. While this means clients don't receive instant push notifications unless they interact with the page or trigger visibility changes, this compromise allowed me to ship a highly performant and secure registry backend in a fraction of the time.
sections.topology_flow_content: The ecosystem integrates a universal DOM-scraping engine embedded in a Chrome sidepanel, communicating with a Supabase PostgreSQL backend. The client utilizes a custom authentication storage adapter via chrome.storage.local, while the frontend employs a custom Zustand store with Page Visibility sync.

sections.code_implementation_content: Leveraging clean TypeScript structures, custom storage bridges, and visibility hooks to ensure synchronicity and visual stability.
sections.resilient_ui_explanation: This custom hook demonstrates a Resilient UI architecture. By integrating the Page Visibility API, the application automatically synchronizes the registry state whenever a user returns to the browser tab. This effectively solves the stale-data problem in collaborative environments (multiple family members claiming gifts) without the overhead or complexity of constant WebSocket connections. It further showcases clean state management through Memoized callbacks and Optimistic UI updates, ensuring a high-performance, real-time feel for the end user.
sections.ux_dom_engine_explanation: Injecting a side panel is a common task, but doing it without breaking 3rd-party site layouts (especially those using 100vw) is difficult. This snippet shows a sophisticated CSS injection strategy using padding-right and box-sizing: border-box. It proves deep mastery of the CSS Box Model, manipulating the host page’s global layout without introducing layout shifts or side-scrolling bugs.
sections.performance_bottlenecks_content: A key bottleneck was injecting the extension's UI elements on third-party sites without breaking their existing styles. I solved this by leveraging non-destructive CSS box-model manipulation to push host contents smoothly. Furthermore, to avoid overloading active tabs, the DOM scraping engine only activates when the user explicitly triggers the sidepanel.
sections.beta_testing_content: The universal registry is fully deployed and operational at petitpals.app. I am actively looking for pilot families and early testers to gather real-world usage feedback and prioritize the next batch of feature integrations.
sections.technical_benchmarks_content: The custom scraping engine successfully processes product metadata across a wide range of platforms with a 100% success rate on clean JSON-LD sites. Cross-context client state updates sync with a sub-100ms latency on active connections.
sections.key_takeaways_content: Direct DOM manipulation taught me the critical importance of defensive CSS design when building extensions. On the product side, prioritizing guest user experience by removing login requirements resulted in a significant boost in reservation completion rates.
sections.future_roadmap_content: Future plans include adding automated price drop tracking and alerts, multi-retailer unified checkout capabilities, and private sharing controls for sensitive baby registries.

zod_schema_visualizer.title: Zod Schema Visualizer & Generator
zod_schema_visualizer.subtitle: An AI-powered developer tool for bridging the gap between type-safe schemas and dynamic UI generation.

generation.label: AI Generation Speed
generation.desc: Sub-second schema generation using Llama 3.3 via Groq.

type_safety.label: Type Accuracy
type_safety.desc: Recursive AST-like traversal for accurate Zod-to-TS conversion.

render_perf.label: UI Frame Rate
render_perf.desc: Throttled token buffering to prevent React render saturation.

sections.project_origin_content: The Zod Schema Visualizer is a technical demonstration designed to bridge the gap between backend validation schemas and frontend UI implementation. It allows developers to define complex data structures via Zod and instantly generate interactive, validated React forms. By integrating AI-driven schema generation, the tool transforms a vague prompt (e.g., 'a user profile with social links') into a robust, type-safe validation object and a corresponding functional sandbox.
sections.learning_objectives_content: My primary goals were to design a highly optimized React form mapper and implement advanced streaming buffering strategies. I wanted to deepen my understanding of AST-like recursive traversal for TypeScript generation and construct edge-ready AI pipelines that handle real-time streaming tokens without saturating the client's rendering loop.
sections.workplace_frustration_content: In modern full-stack development, maintaining synchronization between validation logic (Zod), TypeScript types, and UI forms is a frequent source of technical debt and bugs. Manually building accessible, validated forms for nested or conditional schemas is repetitive and error-prone. Furthermore, prototyping these structures often requires a local setup, slowing down the ideation phase for developers.
behavioral_insights_list: 🛑 Manual form-to-schema synchronization leading to validation drift.
🛑 High boilerplate overhead when implementing dynamic UI for complex Zod objects.
🛑 UI lag when rendering streaming text from LLMs into reactive React components.
sections.anonymity_challenge_content: Integrating low-latency AI schema generation presented a major hurdle: LLM outputs are unpredictable and can easily break frontend parsing if they don't conform to strict syntactical rules. I resolved this by enforcing OpenAI's Structured Outputs / JSON schema at the LLM boundary and implementing a custom streaming parser that validates schema chunks incrementally.
sections.scoping_mvp_content: To build a useful prototyping tool quickly, I focused the MVP on immediate schema compilation and live form preview. I deferred complex multi-file schema relationships and custom Zod validation refinements to prioritize an elegant, single-schema developer playground with real-time editing response.
sections.tech_debt_content: To ship the MVP rapidly, I routed all AI compilation requests directly through Groq's API via Vercel Edge functions using in-memory rate limits. I chose to bypass full persistent user storage and schema hosting databases, meaning users cannot currently save or share their generated sandboxes via permanent links. This deliberate trade-off significantly simplified backend infrastructure.
sections.topology_flow_content: The architecture comprises a Next.js frontend with Monaco Editor integration, a Vercel Edge backend calling Groq for sub-second streaming, a custom AST-like visitor pattern parser, and a throttled token-flushing state store.

sections.code_implementation_content: Leveraging recursive type mapping and a throttled token queue to deliver optimal render performance under high frequency updates.
sections.ux_dom_engine_explanation: Throttling LLM token updates via a dedicated buffer hook to prevent React render saturation, maintaining a consistent 60fps during schema generation.
sections.resilient_ui_explanation: Implementing a recursive visitor pattern to traverse Zod's internal 'def' tree, ensuring 100% accuracy in generated TypeScript interfaces, including nested structures and optional fields.
sections.performance_bottlenecks_content: A major performance bottleneck was the UI lag during live LLM token streaming, as React re-rendered on every character. I resolved this by building a custom 'Flush Buffer' hook that batches updates to 80ms intervals, ensuring a stable 60fps frame rate and preventing render saturation.
sections.beta_testing_content: The visualizer is fully operational and available for developer testing. I am currently collecting feedback from early adopters in the TypeScript community to shape the next phase of development.
sections.technical_benchmarks_content: The playground generates complex validation objects under 800ms using Groq. The visitor pattern parser outputs TypeScript interfaces with 100% fidelity compared to native Zod output.
sections.key_takeaways_content: Working with streaming UI taught me that high-frequency React updates must be buffered to preserve page responsiveness. I also learned that strict schema enforcement is essential when integrating LLM generators into programmatic tooling.
sections.future_roadmap_content: Upcoming plans include supporting full schema composition (e.g. zod union and intersection), exporting form code compatible with Formik/React Hook Form, and generating mock data matching schemas.

sections.project_origin_content: Ouileep was born out of a specific frustration I experienced alongside my colleagues at work. Traditional 360-degree performance reviews felt exhausting and suffered from severe recency bias—managers only remembered the last two weeks of a quarter. I wanted to build an AI-powered alternative that captures unstructured daily team data and logs text updates cleanly directly inside Slack, keeping an honest and automatic record of our contributions.
sections.learning_objectives_content: Beyond solving this workplace issue, my goal for Ouileep was to push my full-stack execution from '0 to 100' as a solo developer. Having seen how architectural choices drive business outcomes in my previous roles, I wanted to deliberately apply that experience here—taking ownership of the entire product life cycle and proving I can independently design an infrastructure that balances engineering speed with real product utility.
sections.workplace_frustration_content: Observing how my team interacted with existing HR systems revealed why continuous feedback fails in most companies. Forcing developers to leave their terminal and Slack workspace to log achievements in an external portal meant it simply never got done. Complex workflows created a high cognitive load, causing people to skip giving feedback entirely.
sections.anonymity_challenge_content: While building the app, I ran into a critical product challenge: team members will not share honest insights or ideas unless they feel safe, yet managers need to know who to help when a project stalls. I solved this by designing a conditional privacy pipeline. Ideas, suggestions, and wins are fully anonymized at the API gateway to protect user identity. However, when an employee logs a blocker, the system explicitly preserves their name in the manager's AI digest so leadership can immediately step in and unblock the right person.
sections.scoping_mvp_content:
To get a working version out as quickly as possible, I focused strictly on simple Slack slash commands
 (/win, /block, /suggest) and a clean Next.js dashboard for managers to view aggregated entries. 
 I purposely skipped complex customization features and advanced graphs to focus entirely on making sure the AI classified text logs reliably and returned data quickly.
sections.tech_debt_content: To accelerate our time-to-market, I coupled a monolithic Next.js structure with a lightweight Hono sub-router and Drizzle ORM for PostgreSQL. I chose to handle incoming Slack webhooks and database writes immediately within these edge-ready serverless routes instead of layering on an asynchronous message queue wrapper like BullMQ. While this architectural shortcut introduces potential connection-pooling and blocking overhead under massive enterprise spikes, it was an intentional trade-off to ship a blazing-fast, end-to-end operational MVP before over-engineering for theoretical scale.
sections.topology_flow_content: The stack consists of a real-time event listener handling Slack webhooks, a Next.js Serverless backend using OpenAI's Structured Outputs to turn messy user text into clean JSON data, a PostgreSQL database, and a lightweight frontend state manager using Zustand to handle instantaneous layout rendering.

sections.code_implementation_content: Using type-safe API endpoints on the backend and a simple state store on the frontend to keep data loading smoothly.
sections.engineering_explanation: This serverless route accepts the text sent from Slack, uses OpenAI's json_schema format to organize the unstructured message into clear categories, and saves it to the database using Prisma.
sections.resilient_ui_explanation: A straightforward Zustand store that manages UI filtering. It updates data instantly on screen to prevent annoying layout shifts or loading delay popping for the user.
sections.performance_bottlenecks_content: The main performance issue I faced was the combined delay of serverless cold-starts and OpenAI API response times. To keep the app feeling fast, I optimized my database indexes for quicker lookups and built optimistic UI updates on the frontend so the dashboard updates instantly before the server even finishes responding.
sections.beta_testing_content: The full-stack application is complete and fully functional. Because this is a pre-launch product, I am currently looking for early-access testing partners—ideally small tech startups or engineering teams with 10+ developers and dedicated product leads—to test the app in a real environment and give me feedback.
sections.technical_benchmarks_content: During my own testing using simulated user data, the app maintained a sub-200ms response acknowledgment time back to Slack. The AI formatting layer successfully categorized and tagged text logs with a stable 94.2% accuracy rate.
sections.key_takeaways_content: Building this taught me that meeting users inside their existing workspaces (Slack) is much more effective than forcing them to adopt secondary tracking platforms. From an architecture standpoint, enforcing strict schemas at the AI boundary is critical for guaranteeing predictable frontend UI states.
sections.future_roadmap_content: Next, I plan to support interactive Slack modals for an even better user experience, add basic automated weekly email summaries for managers, and integrate with GitHub webhooks to automatically suggest log entries whenever a developer merges a Pull Request.
